# The "Doves"
The [bold]Hearts and Minds Movement[/bold] (HMM), known to the average servicemember as the [bold]Doves[/bold], is the faction within the UA's militaries that believes they exist to keep the peace, not to wage war.
## History - The HMM began as a UA political movement after the Tientsin Campaign of 2162-2165, which ended in a tactical nuclear exchange between UPP and USCM forces on 8 Eta Bootis A III. Its founders were sickened by the civilian toll of a campaign that gained nothing, and argued that diplomacy and winning over the local population would have ended it far sooner. - It has since spread through the UA government and every branch of its military, and is especially strong in the LACN and the USCM.
## Ideology [italic]These are the faction's general attitudes. Individual members may hold only some of them.[/italic] - [bold]Alignment[/bold]: progressive, humanitarian, anti-war and peacekeeping. Non-corporate. - Attempt a diplomatic solution whenever possible. - Minimize civilian casualties. Indiscriminate bombardment and heavy damage to civilians or their infrastructure is unacceptable. - Win the cooperation of locals, whether as interpreters, informants or even armed, friendly militias. - Provide humanitarian aid, from water treatment and rations to construction work. - The military's duty is to keep the peace. When violence is needed, it should remove only those harming the general population.
## Internal Divisions The HMM thrives on its open, decentralized nature, but that has also split it. The [bold]old guard[/bold], born of the horrors of Tientsin, sees the military's true strength in its restraint. A newer wave of reformists backs controversial ideas, such as merging the UA's militaries into a single federal force, that have alienated many of the movement's founders.
## Reputation - Colonies that receive HMM aid often see it as the rare compassionate face of the UA military. Water purification, airdrops of food and medicine, and engineering support have visibly improved life on several outer colonies, and HMM patrols have made pirate-plagued trade routes safe again, capturing pirates rather than killing them where they can. - Critics in government and high command call its projects small, slow "band-aid fixes" that never address deeper problems, and hard evidence of their success is scarce. - As the [textlink="Colonial Liberation Front" link="CMUGuideLoreCLF"] (CLF) spreads through the Neroid Sector, the HMM's approach is increasingly called dangerously naive. Several aid convoys and supply drops have been seized by the CLF, pirates and insurgents and sold on the black market, and calls to suspend aid in contested zones are growing.
## Relations - [textlink="The Hawks" link="CMUGuideLoreUAHawks"]: bitter rivals. The Doves see Hawk tactics as destroying any chance of winning colonists over, and often push for courts-martial and war crimes tribunals against them, though the evidence is usually weak or missing. - [textlink="The Magpies" link="CMUGuideLoreUAMagpies"]: wary. The Doves oppose corporations that push ever deadlier weapons, but work with those that make humanitarian and survival equipment, and welcome anything that keeps troops alive.
